  • link it to a different object with the "Link" button.
  • delete it with the button, after confirming. This removes the link between the object and the image, but not the object itself.

Press Escape, or click the "Clear selection" button, to clear the selection and leave draw mode.

Regions can also be used with the keyboard: press Tab to move between them and Enter or Space to select one in edit mode, or to open the linked object in the full-screen view.

docs.title: Tags
docs.text: Tags are labels that can be applied to any object in the Gramps database – people, families, events, places, sources, citations, repositories, notes, and media. They are useful for grouping and filtering objects. Tags are stored in the Gramps family tree database and are shared across all users; they are also fully compatible with tags created in Gramps Desktop.

docs.title: Managing tags
docs.text:
Tags are managed from the Tags section of Administration Settings, which is only available to users with the Owner or Administrator role. It shows all existing tags and allows you to:

  • Create a new tag using the New Tag button
  • Rename a tag using the edit (pencil) icon
  • Change the colour of a tag using the colour picker
  • Delete a tag using the delete icon

Note

Deleting a tag removes it from all objects it was applied to.

docs.title: Applying tags to objects
docs.text:
Tags can be applied to or removed from an object on its detail page when in edit mode. To tag many objects at once, select them in a list and use the Add Tag or Remove Tag action, see Lists.

Tags are shown in the Tags column of the lists, and in search results, bookmarks, and history. If a list does not show the column, enable it in the column picker.

docs.title: Filtering by tag
docs.text: All object list pages (People, Families, Events, Places, Sources, Citations, Repositories, Notes, Media) include a tag filter. Use it to show only objects that have a specific tag applied.

docs.title: Special tags
docs.text:
Two tags have a special meaning in Gramps Web:

  • Blog – any source tagged Blog is treated as a blog post and appears in the Blog view
  • ToDo – any note tagged ToDo is treated as a research task and appears in the Tasks view

These tags are created automatically when you first use the Blog or Tasks features. Renaming or deleting them will break the corresponding feature.

docs.title: Use the built-in task management
docs.text: Gramps Web contains a built-in genealogical task management tool. It is meant to enable researchers to plan and prioritize, but also document their tasks. This is why tasks are represented as sources in the Gramps database. After completing a task, the associated content can serve as a source documenting the research process.

docs.title: Task basics
docs.text:
Tasks have the following properties:

  • Status. This can be "Open", "In Progress", "Blocked", or "Done"
  • Priority. This can be "Low", "Medium", or "High"
  • Tags. The labels are normal Gramps tags of the underlying source. (Note that all tasks additionally have the ToDo label to identify them as tasks, but this label is hidden in the task list to avoid clutter.)
  • Title. Shown in the task list
  • Description. A rich-text field that can be used to describe the problem statement, but also document any progress made
  • Media. Any media files attached to the task

docs.title: Create a task
docs.text:
Since tasks are normal Gramps objects, they can be edited or created by the same group of users that can edit or create other objects (like people or events).

To create a task, click on the + button on the task list page. Enter at least a title, and optionally a priority, a description, attachments, and tags. The status will always be "Open" on creation.

docs.title: The task list
docs.text:
By default, the task list is sorted by status – done tasks last – and within each status by priority, highest first. The sort menu in the filter bar also sorts by priority, title, or last change (newest first).

Click a task to open it. Users with edit permissions can also click the status icon of a task to change its status directly in the list, for example to mark it as done.

The filter button above the list filters the tasks by title, status, priority, or tag, with a GOQL expression, or with the advanced filter. Ticking several statuses or priorities shows tasks with any of them, for example all open and blocked tasks.

docs.title: Edit a task
docs.text:
The task page does not have a separate "edit mode" like other Gramps objects:

  • Click the title to edit it. Press Enter, click ✓, or click elsewhere to save; press Escape or click ✕ to cancel.
  • Changes to the status and priority are applied immediately.
  • To edit the description or the attachments, click the edit button next to the heading of the section. The description is saved with the "save" button beneath it; editing attachments ends with Done.
  • The lock button sets whether the task is private. The task's description gets the same privacy.

Users without edit permissions see the status and priority as text, and sections without content are hidden.

Below the title, editors see two more buttons: Edit Source opens the source that represents the task, where its other notes, citations, and attributes can be edited. Delete deletes the task after a confirmation and returns to the task list; the message that appears has an undo button to restore the task.

docs.title: Bulk change of task properties
docs.text: Users with edit permissions see a checkbox on each row of the task list. Select tasks and use Set Priority or Set Status above the list to change all selected tasks at once.

docs.title: Tasks in Gramps Desktop
docs.text:
When adding tasks via Gramps Web, both the sources and the notes will have the ToDo tag attached to them, so the tasks will show up in the desktop To Do Notes Gramplet as well as the To Do Report.

To add or edit a task in Gramps Desktop, use the following guidelines

  • Add a source with tag ToDo and the task title as title
  • Optionally, add a note to the source with tag ToDo, type "To Do", and the description as text
  • Add an attribute "Status" and set it to "Open", "In Progress", "Blocked", or "Done"
  • Add an attribute "Priority" and set it to 9 for low, 5 for medium, or 1 for high (these counter-intuitive values are taken from the iCalendar specification)

docs.title: Timeline
docs.text:
Info

The Timeline view requires a sufficiently recent Gramps Web API version. If your server is older, the Timeline item is hidden from the sidebar.

Timeline is a sidebar item that shows all events in your family tree laid out chronologically on a horizontal, zoomable timeline.

docs.title: Browsing the timeline
docs.text:
• Scroll, drag, or pinch to move through time; use the zoom buttons (or your mouse wheel/pinch gesture) to zoom in and out.
  • As you zoom in, event labels appear; click an event dot to see its details (and those of any other events on the same date).

docs.title: Filtering
docs.text:
Use the filter field to focus the timeline on a single person or place:

  • Person – shows only events linked to that person, including the events of their families, such as marriages. A toggle lets you switch between Person (events of that individual only), Ancestors, and Descendants (events of all their ancestors/descendants).
  • Place – shows only events that took place there.

Clear the filter chip to return to the full timeline.

docs.title: Jumping to the timeline
docs.text: On an event's or place's detail page, the Show on timeline button opens the Timeline view scrolled and zoomed to that event's date.

docs.title: Editing the Family Tree
docs.text:
The Ancestor Tree view offers a quick way to build and extend the structure of your family tree directly from the chart, without leaving the tree view.

Note

Tree editing is available in the Ancestor Tree, Descendant Tree, Hourglass Graph, and Relationship Graph tabs. It is not available in the Fan Chart. Only users with the Editor role or above can use it.

docs.title: Entering and exiting edit mode
docs.text:
Users with edit permissions see a floating pencil button (bottom right) on supported chart pages. Click it to enter edit mode – or press the e keyboard shortcut. The app bar will show an edit mode indicator.

Each change (adding or linking a person) is saved to the database immediately when confirmed in the dialog. To exit edit mode, click the close button in the app bar, or switch to a different chart tab.

Note

Switching chart tabs automatically exits edit mode.

docs.title: Adding a family member
docs.text:
In edit mode, each person card in the chart shows a small + button. Clicking it opens the Add Family Member dialog for that person, with one or two icons for each available relationship:

  • Father – only shown if the person has no father yet in their primary parent family
  • Mother – only shown if the person has no mother yet in their primary parent family
  • Child
  • Spouse

Each relationship offers two options side by side:

  • Link icon – connect an existing person already in the database
  • + icon – create a brand new person

docs.title: Linking an existing person
docs.text:
Choose the link icon and search for the person by name. Select them from the results to create the family link.

For a child, you can also set the relationship type to father and mother (Birth, Adopted, Stepchild, etc.).

For a spouse, you can set the family relationship type (Married, Civil Union, Unknown, etc.).

docs.title: Creating a new person
docs.text:
Choose the + icon to open a minimal creation form. The fields available are:

  • Name (given name and surname)
  • Gender (Unknown, Male, Female, Other)
  • Birth date and place
  • Death date and place

The new person is saved and immediately linked to the selected person in the chart.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
The tree edit view is for quickly building the skeleton of a family tree. Use the person's detail page for anything beyond the basics: citations, notes, media, attributes, alternate names, existing event details, multiple parent families (only the primary family is accessible here), and managing multiple spouses.

Use Person Details (the account card icon in the toolbar) to jump directly to the full edit view of the currently centred person.

docs.title: Family Tree
docs.text: The Family Tree page is accessible from the sidebar and displays interactive charts centred on a selected person. Five chart types are available via tabs at the top of the page.

docs.title: Selecting the starting person
docs.text:
All charts start from the person currently selected in the tree (shown in the toolbar). The currently centred person is highlighted with a drop shadow. Use the Home Person button to jump back to your home person, or the Back button to return to the previously viewed person. Clicking a person's card in any chart re-centres the chart on that person.

If no home person has been set, the page offers a Set Home Person button to search for and select one directly. If the tree does not contain any people yet, users with the Editor role or above instead see a New Person button – the first person created in an empty tree automatically becomes your home person, so the chart is shown straight away.

docs.title: Ancestor Tree
docs.text: A pedigree chart showing the ancestors of the selected person. Parents appear to the left (or right, depending on layout), grandparents further out, and so on.

docs.title: Descendant Tree
docs.text: Shows the descendants of the selected person – children, grandchildren, and so on.

docs.title: Hourglass Graph
docs.text: Combines ancestors above and descendants below the selected person in a single view.

docs.title: Relationship Graph
docs.text:
Shows the relationship path between two people. The selected person is one endpoint; click any other person in the chart to set the second endpoint and display the shortest relationship path between them.

Each couple is joined by a small family node between the two partners. Hover over it, or click or tap it, to see the family's details – such as the marriage date and place and the children – without leaving the chart. The Open button in the preview leads to the family's page. The node of a couple who are not married has a dashed outline.

Note

The same person may appear more than once in the graph – for example when someone has been married multiple times and appears in several family units along the path. This is intentional, not a bug.

docs.title: Fan Chart
docs.text:
A circular pedigree chart. Ancestors radiate outward from the selected person at the centre.

The Color button in the toolbar colours the segments by a property of each person: the number of events or notes, birth year, death year, age, surname, religion, or ancestor frequency (how often a person appears in the chart). Colouring by surname uses the surname of the person's birth name, or of the primary name if there is no birth name. To remove the colouring, clear the chip that shows the chosen colour.

docs.title: Moving to relatives and expanding branches
docs.text:
In the Ancestor Tree and the Fan Chart, the selected person has a chevron button that opens a menu of their children. In the Descendant Tree, it opens a menu of their parents instead. Choosing a person from the menu centres the chart on them.

In the Ancestor Tree, Descendant Tree and Hourglass Graph, people at the edge of the chart whose parents or children are not shown have a chevron on the side where their branch continues. Clicking it adds one more generation to that branch, while the selected person stays the same. This way, you can for example look at all grandparents and then follow just one line further back. Expanded branches are reset when you select another person or switch to a different chart.

docs.title: Navigation controls
docs.text:
All chart types share a toolbar with the following buttons:

  • Home Person – jump back to your home person
  • Back – go back to the previously centred person
  • Person Details – open the full profile page of the currently centred person
  • Preferences – open a dialog to adjust chart-specific display options (see below)

All charts support pan (click and drag) and zoom (scroll wheel or pinch).

docs.title: Chart preferences
docs.text:
The Preferences dialog (gear icon in the toolbar) lets you adjust the following options, depending on the chart type:

  • Max Ancestor Generations – how many generations of ancestors to display
  • Max Descendant Generations – how many generations of descendants to display
  • Max Degree of Separation – for the Relationship Graph, the maximum path length to search. High values can make the chart slow to load on large trees.
  • Max Number of Images displayed – limits profile photos shown in the chart for performance
  • Name Display Format – controls how names are shown on person cards

Click Reset to restore the defaults, or Close to apply your changes.

Chart preference settings are stored in the browser's local storage, so they persist across sessions on the same device.

docs.title: Default chart type
docs.text: The chart type shown when you first open the Family Tree page can be configured in User Settings. Your chosen default applies on all your devices.

docs.title: Editing the tree
docs.text: Users with the Editor role or above can add and link people directly from the Ancestor Tree. See Editing the family tree for details.

docs.title: Using Gramps Web for Y-DNA Analysis
docs.text:
Note

This feature requires Gramps Web API version 3.3.0 or later and Gramps Web frontend version 25.9.0 or later.

The Y-DNA view in Gramps Web can use raw Y chromosome single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) data to determine a person's most likely Y-DNA haplogroup and display the derived ancestors in the human Y chromosome tree along with timing estimates.

docs.title: How to obtain and store the Y-DNA SNP data
docs.text:
To obtain the Y-DNA SNP data, you need to have a Y-DNA test performed through a genetic testing service. The result is represented as a set of mutations (SNPs), each identified by a string (e.g. R-BY44535) and a + or - sign indicating whether the mutation is present or absent. Gramps Web expects the string of all tested SNPs in the format SNP1+, SNP2-, SNP3+,... to be stored in a person attribute of custom type Y-DNA (case sensitive). You can either manually create this attribute in Gramps Web or Gramps Desktop, or navigate to the Y-DNA view in Gramps Web and click the blue "Add" button, select the person to add the data to, and paste the SNP string. In any case, the data will be stored as a person attribute in your Gramps database.

See below for instructions on how to obtain the SNP data from various testing services.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
Once a person has a Y-DNA attribute containing the SNP data, Gramps Web will use the open-source yclade Python library to determine the person's most likely position on the human Y chromosome tree. The tree has been created by the YFull project based on tens of thousands of Y-DNA tests. Note that Gramps Web uses a local copy of the YFull tree, so no data is sent to any third party.

The tree is traversed from the root to the leaves, and at each node, the SNPs associated with that node are compared to the person's positively and negatively tested SNPs, and the appropriate branch is followed.

The final result is a succession of clades from the root of the tree (the Y-chromosomal "Adam") to the most derived clade that is consistent with the person's SNP data. Each clade has an estimated age based on the ages of the samples in the YFull database that belong to that clade.

Since Y chromosomes are inherited from father to son, this succession corresponds to an excerpt of the person's patrilineal ancestry.

docs.title: How to interpret the results
docs.text:
The most important piece of information is the person's most likely haplogroup, shown at the top of the page. The name is linked to the corresponding page on the YFull website, which contains more information, such as the country of origin of tested samples belonging to that haplogroup.

In the patrineal ancestor tree shown in Gramps Web, the box directly above the tested person is the most recent common ancestor (MRCA) of all tested samples belonging to the person's haplogroup. The date shown for this ancestor is his estimated approximate birth date. The ancestor above him is the ancestor where the mutation defining this haplogroup first appeared.

Due to the slow mutation rate of Y chromosomes, the MRCA can be many hundreds of years in the past. For rare haplogroups (i.e. halogroups where few people have been tested so far), it can even be thousands of years.

Between the MRCA and the tested person, the chart shows the paternal line as far as it is documented in your tree: the father, his father, and so on, oldest first. The dotted line above the oldest documented ancestor stands for the generations that are not documented, with an estimate of their number. Only biological fathers are followed – the line stops at an adoptive father or stepfather, since they did not pass on the Y chromosome. Click a person in the line to open their page.

The icon on each clade box opens that clade on the YFull website.

docs.title: Private Y-DNA data
docs.text: The dialogs for adding and editing Y-DNA data have a Private switch. Private Y-DNA data is hidden from users who can't view private records. See Private records.

docs.title: Instructions for obtaining SNP data from testing services
YSEQ
docs.text: Once logged in to "My Account", go to "My Results / View my Alleles" and navigate to the bottom of the page. The text field " Allele list compact" has been added specifically for Gramps Web and is in exactly the right format for pasting into the Y-DNA attribute.
